research_concepts: teammate DRIVE immediately preceding a PNR possession
derived possession records (initiator, play type, points)
methodological_questions: Can a teammate DRIVE that immediately precedes a PNR be identified reliably from the current derived labels?
Does conditioning on the preceding DRIVE change PNR PPP after adjusting for shot quality, matchup, clock, score and lineup?
Can the precedence test be run without lookahead or outcome-derived labels?
What multiplicity and selection risks arise when a single pair is chosen from many possible teammate sequences?

historical_evidence.finding: Play-type labeling audit found OTHER possessions with 36% foul endings and inflated PPP, DRIVE 12pp below the foul benchmark, PNR with a 22% foul rate, and only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) mapping to a real play type via initiation_type.

Play-type label accuracy audit overall FAIL: OTHER 20.2% against a <10% target, 40.8% low-confidence labels, DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark, most play types with PPP above the benchmark band, and MIA identity checks failing.

Backfill verification: PNR share 28.7% FAIL against a 20-28% band, PULL_UP 7.9% FAIL, team identity FAIL, and PNR PPP 0.948 PASS; 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated; final result FAIL over 921,514 possessions.

Season-stability test of top suppressors and negative teammate pairs: only 2/30 stars met the 75% same-top-suppressor rule. Reported negative pair premiums included Giannis->Lillard DRIVE->PNR -0.263 (n=31), which is the only record here with a DRIVE->PNR teammate sequence.
On-ball coverage labels could be assigned to only 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of on-ball half-court possessions; switches_on was unpopulated; verdict failed_gate.
Adaptation falsification (asymmetry, confidence and carryover tests) was flagged as C_artifact with LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR risks; the next-game PPP test was Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842.
Opponent-play-before-star suppression: PUTBACK was the top suppressor for 6+ stars (e.g. D. Mitchell d=-0.294, n_after=95), with n_after 32-95 in several cells and no multiplicity correction.
Regular-season vs playoff PPP by play type: DRIVE RS 1.198 vs PO 0.912 (-0.286, 25 teams); PNR -0.173. Team-level cells with min 30 possessions; no CIs.

Star suppression by lineup and forced play type, with lineup cells of n=30-59 and a min-15 gate on 8 play types. No placebo or matching was done, and later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
PBP-derived PNR shot-level shares for 2024-25 (for example OKC 7.567%, IND 13.824%) were a calibration input for PBPProxyPNR; no pass/fail gate in the output.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using initiation_type to attach real play types to possessions for play-type PPP comparisons.
failed_approaches.why: Only 0.7% of 50,668 possessions mapped to a real play type; foul endings inflated OTHER PPP and depressed DRIVE, so PPP differences were recorded as labeling artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type label audit against volume, foul-rate, PPP and team-identity benchmarks.
failed_approaches.why: Labels failed multiple benchmarks (OTHER 20.2%, 40.8% low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw 1.7%); recorded mechanism was a C_artifact with foul possessions leaking into OTHER.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Backfilled play-type labels for PNR and PULL_UP.
failed_approaches.why: Shares and team identity failed; 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated rather than directly observed, so the PNR label is partly model-derived.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Defensive scheme labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from matchup data.
failed_approaches.why: Labeled coverage 14.9% and 3.3%; switches_on unpopulated; failed_gate with recorded mechanism A_unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Season-stable sequential suppressor and negative teammate pair claims.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as rejected (B_powered_null) with 2/30 stable; the DRIVE->PNR pair premium was not stable in the reported analysis.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Opponent-play-before-star suppression tests with cell-level effects.
failed_approaches.why: Small n_after cells (32-95), no multiplicity correction, and DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY risk recorded.

evidence_establishes: The derived play-type labels in this project have been recorded as failing label-accuracy and backfill audits, so any DRIVE and PNR identification built on them has not been validated.
Sequential teammate-pair effects were tested before in this project and recorded as not stable across seasons, which is a caution against an unadjusted single-pair claim.
A DRIVE->PNR teammate pair premium was reported in the project once (Giannis->Lillard, -0.263, n=31), but within a rejected family. It is a single pair and is not a test of the stated question.
Play-type PPP is known to differ between regular season and playoffs, with DRIVE and PNR differences recorded (SF-APPS-011), so season context must be controlled.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests whether a teammate DRIVE immediately preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP.
No record gives a validated count of DRIVE->PNR sequences or a power calculation for them.
The retrieved records do not show whether the PNR PPP gap is real efficiency or a labeling, foul or mechanical artifact.
The direction and size of any effect across seasons remain unknown; the one reported negative premium is a single pair in a rejected family.
own_inferences: The question's central variable, a teammate DRIVE immediately before a PNR, depends on the labels that have failed audits. The test would measure label artifacts as much as basketball.
A DRIVE-to-PNR transition can also be produced by a DRIVE foul or by a possession being relabeled after the fact, so the precedence claim may leak outcome information.
Raising PNR PPP through a preceding drive could be confounded by shot quality, the defender who is moved, the rotation and the clock; none of these are controlled in the retrieved records.
Searching across teammate pairs to find one that raises PNR PPP would create a multiplicity problem similar to the one recorded in SF-APPA-050.
uncertainties: The records do not give the count of teammate DRIVE->PNR pairs per season.
It is unknown whether the derived possession graph can order possessions within a game reliably (the record does not state this).
The label status of PNR in the 2025-26 partial season is not recorded.
The retrieved records do not specify whether the label audits were rerun after any fix.

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval the plan was a direct test. The records show that the play-type labels driving the DRIVE and PNR definitions failed audit (SF-APPM-014, SF-CHT-025, SF-APPA-030), that sequence premiums were not stable (SF-APPA-058), and that sequence-based claims produced artifacts (SF-APPA-050, SF-CHT-009). Together these make a direct test unsafe until labels are validated, so the decision moved from a possible proceed to do_not_proceed.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type labels failed multiple audits and only 0.7% of possessions mapped via initiation_type; the DRIVE and PNR identities are not validated.
PNR labels are 82.8% proxy_calibrated, so some labels may be derived from outcome information.
Possession ordering and labels in the derived records may use information from the same possession's points, so the precedence definition must be checked for lookahead.
Shot quality, matchup, clock, score, lineup and season context all affect PNR PPP and are not controlled in the retrieved records.
Specific DRIVE->PNR teammate pairs are rare; the one reported pair had n=31.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved study directly tests a preceding teammate DRIVE and PNR PPP. SF-APPA-058 reports one DRIVE->PNR pair premium (-0.263, n=31) inside a rejected stability family, and SF-APPA-050 and SF-CHT-009 treat sequential star-chain gaps as weak or artifact-prone. The label audits (SF-APPM-014, SF-APPA-030, SF-CHT-025) show the required variables are not validated, so the question is only partly addressed.

risks.text: Labels failed audit; DRIVE and PNR identity and foul leakage into OTHER may drive any measured gap.
PNR labels are proxy_calibrated (82.8%), so the PNR class may partly reflect outcomes.
Sequence definitions in the derived graph may use same-possession outcome data when deciding that a DRIVE preceded a PNR.
Shot quality, defender matchup, clock, score, lineup and season stage are uncontrolled; the playoff-versus-regular-season PPP gap is recorded for DRIVE and PNR (SF-APPS-011).
Single teammate pair cells can be small (n=31 in the reported example); no power calculation exists.
Many teammate DRIVE->PNR pairs will have too few possessions for stable PPP estimates.
Searching over teammate pairs and play-type pairs without correction would yield false positives, as in SF-APPA-050.
SF-CHT-009 had no placebo; a gap can appear without a placebo control, so a placebo lag is needed.
Seasons and rotation patterns differ across 2022-23 to 2025-26; SF-APPA-050 flagged drift.
PNR PPP baseline differs by team and season; a small preceding-drive effect may be swamped by baseline variation.

design.estimand: Within-team, within-season difference in PNR PPP between PNR possessions immediately preceded by a teammate DRIVE and PNR possessions not so preceded, adjusted for shot quality, defender matchup, clock, score margin, lineup and player fixed effects. This is only a minimum viable test after label validation; it is not run now.
design.unit: PNR possession with its immediately preceding offensive possession, for the same team and game.
design.sample: Regular-season 2022-23 to 2024-25 only, frozen snapshot; 2025-26 regular season only after it is complete (from 2026-04-13); playoffs excluded from the primary test and analysed separately (SF-APPS-011 shows a context effect). Requires a hand-audited sample of labeled DRIVE and PNR possessions before the main test.
design.power: Not computed in the retrieved records. Before running, compute the detectable effect for the expected count of DRIVE->PNR pairs; if the count is near the SF-APPA-058 example (n about 31), the test is underpowered and should not be run for individual pairs.
design.controls: Shot distance and result, defender matchup minutes and partial possessions, clock and period, score margin, starters and rotation intervals, lineup fixed effects, player and team-season fixed effects, regular season versus playoffs indicator.
design.falsification: Placebo lag: DRIVE two possessions before the PNR and an opponent DRIVE before the PNR. Negative-control outcome: DRIVE-to-PNR effect on non-PNR possession PPP. A precedence effect should disappear on both controls.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify one primary pair family (teammate DRIVE immediately preceding PNR). Apply Holm correction across any additional teammate pairs or play types.
design.decision_rule: Conclude a positive effect only if the adjusted difference has a 95% CI excluding zero, survives the placebo and negative-control checks, and the labels pass a pre-registered audit on the same sample. Otherwise report artifact, uncertain or null, as applicable.
design.data_version: Frozen NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season, with the play-type label version recorded and the proxy_calibrated PNR share reported; 2025-26 regular season only after 2026-04-13; playoffs excluded from primary analysis.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
